title: Kiln's registry stage (<game>/kiln/state/registry.json), format 1
description: What a start's registry stage did: for every field a mod's registry edit (or one of Kiln's older paths under it) touched, the base value and where it came from, every writer in the order they apply (Kiln's older paths and archive-writer packages below, then the registry's edits by stage and load order), the result and who decided it; every conflict line with its certainty; every refused edit with its reason. Written by kiln.content (the registry stage: native/services/content/registry/report.cpp report_json) at phase start (restart fields final) and again at worldLoad (every field applied; the generation grows), atomically (a temporary file, then a rename). Readers: the launcher (the Conflicts view, registry P2), kilnctl, support reports. A file whose pid is not a live process is the last start's. Large mod sets: rows past a cap (20,000 fields, 2,000 conflicts, 2,000 refused edits, 20,000 added or removed entries) are left out and counted under truncated; counts always has the totals. kiln.log carries at most 50 of the lines per start and a total. Within format 1 Kiln only adds members: a reader ignores members it does not know.

pid.description: The game's process id as the game sees it (under Proton, the Windows pid).

kiln.description: Kiln version of the runtime that wrote it.

generation.description: kiln.registry's generation (kiln_registry.h KilnRegistryStatus.generation): 1 at start, then +1 at each world load, re-application and live change.

phase.description: At start, restart fields are final and live fields have been composed. At worldLoad, the report includes live values after world load or a pack reload. Late drop tables refresh within the current generation.

regmap.description: Kiln's map of the registries onto this game build (regmap/<side>/<exe sha256>.json). Without a verified record every field is unproven and every edit of it refused.

record.description: The record used, relative to Kiln's folder; null when this build has none.

base.description: What the stage read as its base.

origin.description: live: kiln.assets' bytes at resources-ready (the game's data as the archive writer published it). Later releases may add origins.

writer.description: This start's archive writer: kiln-eml (its EML pass, or Kiln's interpreter in kiln mode), shroudforge-hosted or shroudforge-installed (ShroudForge reserved the startup data writer), external (another loader's proxy ran, or the game data differs from kiln-eml's vanilla backup and is not its output), or none (the game's data as shipped, as far as kiln-eml can tell). Before 0.2.0-dev.31.18 only a kiln-mode start said kiln-eml; every other start said none, also where kiln-eml or hosted ShroudForge had patched the archive. base.archive says what it rests on.

token.description: The archive writer's publication token, when it has one.

archive.description: What Kiln knows the archive writer did this start and what that rests on (since 0.2.0-dev.31.18): kiln-eml's state (kiln/state/eml.json, through kiln.eml) and the names of kiln-eml's ownership receipt and ShroudForge's record of its pass, never their contents.

source.description: kiln-eml: kiln-eml's state of this start; none: kiln-eml did not answer (no kiln-eml, or an older one).

phase.description: kiln-eml's phase: done, aside, idle, failed.

patched.description: Resources kiln-eml's run patched this start.

cached.description: kiln-eml found nothing changed since its last run: the archive keeps its patches.

restored.description: kiln-eml put the game's own data back from its vanilla backup.

receipt.description: kiln-eml's ownership receipt of what it published (kiln/eml/ownership/<stem>.json), relative to the game folder; null when it is not there.

record.description: ShroudForge's record of its startup pass (<stem>.kfc.prepared.json), relative to the game folder, named only (Kiln never reads it); null when it is not there.

text.description: One English sentence: who published the archive and how Kiln knows.

journal.description: The archive writer's change journal (kiln-eml's <stem>.change-journal.json: format 1 from a kiln-mode start, format 2 (0.2.0-dev.31.18) from an EML start, EML's own pass): read when it is this start's and its packages are named where they wrote (writer rows of kind archiveWriter, certainty named; format 1 per entry, on registries whose entries are each a whole resource only: items, drops, balance, never a recipe or loot entry; format 2 per field from its member paths, recipe and loot entries by their element); none when this start has none (hosted or installed ShroudForge and other loaders keep none: what they changed is part of the base, unnamed); stale when the file names another generation; unreadable when it is not a journal of format 1 or 2. Since 0.2.0-dev.31.17 (format 2: 0.2.0-dev.31.18).

packages.description: The packages the journal lists (0 unless read).

entries.description: The registry entries of this start's base it named.

truncated.description: The journal left entries out past its bounds: a package may have written entries it does not name.

text.description: One English sentence: what was read, or why nothing is named.

order.description: The mods with registry edits, in the order the stage ran them (later wins).

editsHash.description: A hash of the mod's registry inputs (data files and code batches).

orderSource.description: kiln.host: Kiln.Host's runtime load order (the launcher profile's order). folders: no .NET this start, kiln.content's mod folder order.

plan.description: The plan this start runs on (kiln/data/content/registry/plans/<hash>.json, format 2: each mod's lowered edits and the values they resolved to) and previous, the last good plan before it (a world started on it without a refused edit): what kilnctl registry rollback starts the next boot on. Null when none was written.

rollback.description: A rollback asked by kiln/data/content/registry/rollback.json (kilnctl registry rollback): applied (this start runs on that plan's edits instead of the mods' current ones; saves are not touched) or refused whole (its mods are not this start's, its file is missing or changed, or one of its edits is refused on this start: the mods' current edits run). Null: none asked.

changedBack.description: Every value that differs from the plan rolled away from (the first 2,000).

leftOut.description: Mods with registry edits now that the plan does not hold: their edits are not applied while the rollback holds.

madeOnExe.description: The plan was made on another game build (that exe's SHA-256).

saves.description: Registry edits that change what existing saves hold (native/services/content/registry/saves.h): guard (applied, Kiln protects the saves), warn (applied; what saved data means changes, or what the game does is not traced), report (applied; saves follow the new value). Refused ones are in refused. Absent: none.

frontEnds.description: Since 0.2.0-dev.32: this start's front-end documents, a data pack's gearRules (docs/kiln/services/content.md "Gear rules on the registry"). The registry's boot back-end writes such a document's values itself, through Kiln's proven mapping, where that gives the same bytes as its resource patch (compared at this start); its rows stay old-path writers (kind oldPatch, marked frontEnd) in their place below every registry edit. Absent: none.

state.description: registry: the registry's boot back-end wrote its values (the same bytes as its resource patch); resourcePatch: its resource patch wrote them, as before (reason says why).

fields.description: The registry fields its values are (0 when it stayed a resource patch before the stage mapped it).

reason.description: Why it stays a resource patch, in Kiln words.

migrated.description: What the schemas' id migrations (schema/registry/migrations) renamed in this start's edits before they were matched. Absent: nothing.

refused.description: Edits that were not applied, each with its reason (a malformed edit, an unmapped or unproven field, an entry that is not there or was removed by the game build, a conflict with an exclusive edit, a raw path that does not resolve on this build). A reason that starts with the stable token "RestartRequired: " is an edit that waits for the next start (a restart field a reload changed, a field the start never read, a section or entry operation added after the start); counts.restartRequired has their number.

n.description: The edit's ordinal in its batch.

id.description: The entry it was refused on (the one that failed, an exact selector's, an add's), when there is one.

field.description: The Kiln field (or element path, or raw path) it named.

raw.description: Present for an Advanced-tier raw-path refusal, even when its place is unavailable. Readers that do not show raw paths hide field and reason details for these rows only; a field name that is not raw (a misspelled or newer Kiln field) keeps its reason.

restartRequired.description: Refused rows whose reason starts with the stable token "RestartRequired: " (since 0.2.0-dev.31.17): edits a reload, a runtime pass or a live edit left for the next start. Counted over every row, also those the refused cap leaves out.

truncated.description: Rows left out of each list because of its cap (0: none).

writers.description: Writers left out of field rows (each row keeps its last 64; writersLeftOut counts the rest per row).

bootSync.description: Immutable successful client-needed boot registry values and participating mod-order hashes. Optional for old writers, and absent when this start could not apply its side-both mods' client-held boot edits as asked (then nothing is compared at joins: docs/kiln/network.md); full hashes are computed before report caps. Neither server-only fields nor live layers contribute.

value.description: A field's value can be a number, boolean, name, id, or array of list entries. A missing value is null.

field.description: The Kiln field, or (raw: true) the game member path as the first edit wrote it.

raw.description: An Advanced-tier raw member path (owner decision D5): works while the game's names hold.

applies.description: When a change of the field takes effect (the schema's applies).

entriesLeftOut.description: Entries omitted after the first 64 in a base list.

origin.description: archive: the game's data as the archive writer published it; added: an entry a mod added (its base is its like entry's). Later releases may name more origins; show an unknown one as it is.

writers.description: In the order they apply; the last one decided the result.

resultEntriesLeftOut.description: Entries omitted after the first 64 in the result list.

formulaInputs.description: Effective formula inputs corresponding to the numeric live result. Power uses damage factor, attack speed factor, minimum level. Armor uses armor share, minimum level.

winner.description: The writer whose row decided the result last; null: the base.

writersLeftOut.description: The earliest writers of this field left out of writers (only its last 64 are listed: the ones that decide the result).

kind.description: archiveWriter: a ShroudForge or EML package that wrote the entry's resource (or, see named, this field) in the archive before Kiln (named from kiln-eml's change journal; its value is the base); oldPatch: an older Kiln boot resource patch; oldPack: an older Kiln data pack; code: a Content.* change made by code; registry: a registry edit. check: the stage's reference check (list elements naming an entry the stage removed, taken out of an entry of a registry whose entries are not removed). drift (since 0.2.0-dev.31.17): the best-effort drift probe found the game's value changed outside Kiln (between the stage's read and Kiln's first write in the world, or after Kiln's layer) with no writer Kiln knows to explain it; who names the suspects Kiln can see, certainty bestEffort.

mod.description: The Kiln mod behind it (absent for an archive-writer package).

who.description: What the writer is called when that is not just the mod: "<mod>: content/<file>", "<mod>/<key>", "<mod or loader's mod>: <Kiln place>" (a code change made through Kiln's content service, also another loader's: "emf:big_stacks: items[game:material_t1_wood_logs].maxStack"; since 0.2.0-dev.31.18, before it the game's item and member), "shroudforge:<package>", "eml:<package>" (an EML mod: of EML's own pass, or an EML package of the kiln-mode startup pass), "kiln-eml:unattributed" (a startup write no package made, or an EML mod whose id the journal cannot name), "outside Kiln (best effort; suspects: ...)" (a drift row).

frontEnd.description: Since 0.2.0-dev.32: this old-path row's value was written by the registry's boot back-end (a front-end, registry.json frontEnds), not by its resource patch.

raw.description: The raw member path, when the row came from an Advanced-tier edit.

named.description: An archiveWriter row (0.2.0-dev.31.18): what kiln-eml's change journal names the package on. entry: it wrote the entry's resource (a format-1 journal, a resource it created, or a format-2 path that names the whole entry), so it is listed on every field of the entry a mod edits; field: a member path it wrote (a format-2 journal of EML's own pass) is this field's or holds it.

element.description: An element edit of this list: the element path ("inputs[2].count", "inputs[*].count", "perks[1]"); op applies to that element or its leaf.

op.description: An absolute write supplies a plain value or array. A relative write supplies an object with mul, add, min, max, raiseOnly, or lowerOnly. Absent on an archiveWriter row: kiln-eml's journal says where the package wrote (the entry, or with a format-2 journal the field: named), never what it did there; the row's value is the archive's, the base.

value.description: The field's value after this writer.

valueEntriesLeftOut.description: Entries omitted after the first 64 in the writer's list value.

opEntriesLeftOut.description: Entries omitted after the first 64 in a list assigned by op.

listEntriesLeftOut.description: Entries omitted after the first 64 in a list operation's operand.

certainty.description: certain: Kiln's own writers; named: an archive-writer package, from its journal; bestEffort: other loaders' DLLs and hooks.

kind.description: overridden: a later absolute value replaced another writer's; composed: relative changes stacked; composedOn: a relative change applied on another writer's value; exclusive: an exclusive conflict (or one place on two scales) refused the later edit; dropped: an edit into an entry another mod removed; yielded: a yield edit skipped a field an earlier writer set.

text.description: One English sentence, as kiln.log has it.

raw.description: Present when the line's place is a raw path (the Advanced tier) rather than a Kiln field.
